reason: The FAQ and the user guide both state that once Object Lock is enabled on a bucket you cannot disable Object Lock or Versioning (the guide says suspend versioning); the display is verbatim.
The quote under 'How does Amazon S3 Object Lock work?' (found in snapshot www/s3/faqs:456) says the same as the claim: a Legal Hold blocks modification or deletion indefinitely until it is removed.
The quote says Governance Mode lets accounts with specific IAM permissions remove WORM protection, and in Compliance Mode no user can remove it, including the root account.
Under the SEC 17a-4(f)(2)(i) / CFTC 1.31(c) notification question, the quote says AWS is not a D3P and that you should select a D3P and name it in your notification to the DEA (your regulator).
The quote names broker-dealers who must keep non-erasable, non-rewritable records under SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511 or CFTC Regulation 1.31.
The quote lists SRR, CRR, replication metrics, RTC and Batch Replication as all supported when replicating from Object Lock buckets.
The quote states that to replicate from Object Lock enabled buckets, the destination bucket must also have Object Lock enabled.
The quote names s3:GetObjectRetention and s3:GetObjectLegalHold on the source bucket in the replication IAM role, and says s3:Get* also satisfies the requirement.
The context names two retention types, fixed and variable. The quote says fixed sets the Retain Until Date, and variable uses an event hold, with S3 setting the date when the hold is released.
The quote says the same as the claim: an object version is protected from deletion or overwriting for a set period or indefinitely, to enforce retention or for compliance.
The quote states that individual objects range from a minimum of 0 bytes to a maximum of 50 TB; units and min/max match.
The quote states that tags replicate with CRR, and that configurations already enabled need new permissions before tags replicate.
The claim text matches the quote, but the scope names S3 One Zone-IA and S3 Express One Zone. The quote only says 'a One Zone storage class' and never lists which classes those are.
The quote states that One Zone-IA stores data redundantly within a single AZ at 20% less cost than S3 Standard-IA.
The quote says One Zone-IA is not resilient to loss of availability or physical loss of an AZ, while Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA and the Glacier classes are designed to withstand it.
The quote supports a 99% available SLA and eleven 9s durability within the AZ. The scope qualifier 'per billing cycle' does not appear in the quote or its context.
The quote lists backup copies, disaster recovery copies and other easily re-creatable data as infrequently accessed uses of One Zone-IA.

Under 'What is AWS PrivateLink for Amazon S3?', the quote says interface endpoints connect on-premises applications to S3 over Direct Connect or VPN, with no public IPs, firewall changes or internet gateway.
The quote states that copying is automatic and asynchronous, and that the buckets can be owned by the same account or different accounts.
The quote states that replication is not available between China Regions and Regions outside China; it works only within the China Regions.
The quote says CRR and SRR can replicate across accounts, and that Ownership Overwrite keeps a distinct ownership stack and gives the destination account ownership.
The quote states that the source account pays all data transfer and the destination account pays the replication PUT requests.

The quotes support 'all encryption types' and the SSE-S3/SSE-KMS/SSE-C list, but the claim presents that list as complete. The same FAQ (encryption options) also names DSSE-KMS as an S3 option, so the claim's list says more than the quotes establish.
The quote says lifecycle actions are not replicated and that you apply the same configuration to both buckets to get the same behavior.
The quotes name the four metrics in the console and CloudWatch, and s3:Replication event notifications for failed objects and the reasons they failed.
The quote states that metrics and events can be enabled for each replication rule and are on by default for RTC-enabled rules.
The quote covers multiple destinations in the same or different Regions. The next sentence in the context says each destination can choose its own storage class, encryption type and RTC.
The quote states that replication rules can copy objects into another storage class, in the same or a different Region.
The quotes list destination storage, the primary copy, replication PUTs and IA retrieval charges, plus inter-Region DTO for CRR and no data transfer charge for SRR.
The quote states that Batch Replication can re-replicate objects that failed to replicate the first time.
The quote states that CRR and SRR are configured at bucket level, shared prefix level, or object level using object tags.
The quote states that versioning must be enabled on both the source and destination buckets to enable replication.
The quote says Requester Pays is for sharing data without paying for others' access, and that bucket owners generally pay for all storage of their bucket.
The quote states that with RTC you get a notification when an object takes more than 15 minutes to replicate, and another when it then succeeds.
The quote gives the 99.9% / 15-minute threshold per Region pair per monthly billing cycle, with a service credit on any object that takes longer than 15 minutes.
The quote states that S3 is secure by default and that, on creation, only you have access to the buckets you create.
The quote states that the largest object that can be uploaded in a single PUT is 5 GB.
The quote states that the SLA provides a service credit when monthly uptime is below the commitment in any billing cycle.
The quote lists the SRR uses: a copy in a separate account in the same Region for sovereignty and compliance, log aggregation, and live replication between test and development environments.
The quote states that S3 encrypts and decrypts while you keep control of the keys. The context adds that you must manage the keys you send to S3.
